quickAnswerHtml: Phunisa is a Bib Gourmand restaurant in the MICHELIN Guide Thailand 2026, located in Surat Thani, in the Khao Hua Kwai area of Phunphin district, with dishes running about 60–300 THB. It's mostly walk-in, so expect to queue outside.

blocks.html:
If there's one restaurant in Surat Thani that nails the idea of "hundred-baht meal, million-baht view," it's Phunisa — a southern Thai restaurant perched on a hill in Khao Hua Kwai subdistrict, Phunphin district. Even the MICHELIN Guide describes the location as "set on a scenic hillside." You sit and eat while looking out over the green mountains all around, and it's not just a pretty view with ordinary food to match — this restaurant already held a Thai Select mark before it went on to earn a Bib Gourmand in the 2025 MICHELIN Guide, and it's kept that status in the 2026 guide too. A Bib Gourmand is MICHELIN's own stamp of approval for "genuinely good food at a price that doesn't hurt," and that fits Phunisa exactly, since dishes here start at just around sixty baht.

The standout that gets people driving up the hill all the way to Phunphin is the natural river prawns from the Tapi River, Surat Thani's main river, which flows through Phunphin district before reaching Ban Don Bay. Tapi River prawns are known for firm, sweet meat and rich roe in a way farmed prawns simply can't match. Beyond the prawns, the menu is genuine home-style southern Thai food that shifts with the season and whatever local ingredients are available. If you're craving that bold, unfussy southern Thai flavor the way it's cooked at home, eating here makes it clear why MICHELIN picked out a restaurant on a hill well outside the city center for its guide.

What makes Phunisa likeable is that it's a genuine Phunphin locals' restaurant, not one built for tourists. Phunphin district is the gateway to Surat Thani, home to both the airport and the Surat Thani train station. If you're flying in or arriving by train to catch a boat to Koh Samui, Koh Phangan, or head to Cheow Lan Dam, this is one of the best spots for your first or last meal before leaving the province. The review scores back up the popularity too — Phunisa ranks number 1 out of 8 restaurants in Phunphin district on TripAdvisor, with a score of 4.3 out of 5. There's a view terrace where you can sit, catch the breeze, and take photos with the mountains behind you before heading out. One meal gets you the river prawns, the view, and genuine southern Thai atmosphere, all at a price that's easy on the wallet.

faq.a: No reservation needed — the restaurant is walk-in only, with no online booking system. If you're coming as a large group or want to check that the restaurant is open, call 080-529-7111 or 080-529-6111. The restaurant accepts Mastercard/Visa.

faq.q: What's the budget per person at Phunisa?
faq.a: Dishes run about 60–300 THB each. Two people can eat well, including river prawns, on a budget of 400–800 THB — fitting for a Bib Gourmand, MICHELIN's award for good food at an accessible price.

faq.q: What should I order at Phunisa?
faq.a: The must-order dish is the natural river prawns from the Tapi River, with firm, sweet meat and rich roe, followed by the home-style southern Thai dishes that rotate with the season and local ingredients.

faq.q: What are Phunisa's hours, and how do I get there?
faq.a: Open daily 11:00–20:00 (last order 19:30), but closed on the 16th–17th of every month. The restaurant sits on a hilltop in Khao Hua Kwai subdistrict, Phunphin district, and can only be reached by car. There's parking on site, and it's not far from Surat Thani's airport and train station.
